agree.reason: It brings up the March deadline error before he can, takes responsibility for it, and points to the fix and the 600 clean entries since, so a partner who doubts her is likely to agree to the meeting and give the request serious thought.

honest.reason: Every figure matches what she supplied, but 'I know how each of them works' glosses over the fact that one of the three trainees left after 8 months.

works_the_facts.reason: The 600 error-free entries are used well, but the hours figure is left bare instead of being stated as 90 hours (about 6%) over target, and nothing is said about how many paralegals she would supervise.

right_comparison.reason: The before-and-after for the sheet, with one person checking alone versus two-person confirmation, is accurate and shows the trend, but the letter never says what the group loses if no one takes on the supervising role.

qualification.reason: The weekly check-ins and certification by June 2027 are concrete and can be checked, and 'I can't promise I'll never make another error' is honest, but no consequence is attached if either commitment slips.

objections.reason: It meets the partner's specific objection directly, admits 'That was too close,' and answers it with the system fix and its record without making excuses.

fit.reason: It is a properly formed promotion request well under 400 words, but it ends with a '[Your name]' placeholder even though her name was available.
